record.paper_title: Research Problems on Relations Between Nijenhuis Geometry and Integrable Systems
record.context_brief: Finite-gap and soliton solutions for BKM systems
record.original_question: Using the finite-dimensional reduction approach described in §2.4, obtain soliton-type solutions for known special cases of BKM systems such as KdV, coupled KdV, Harry Dym, coupled Harry Dym, Camassa–Holm, multi-component Camassa–Holm, Dullin–Gottwald–Holm, and Kaup–Boussinesq, and determine which solutions produced by the method of [13] should count as finite-gap or soliton solutions. In particular, for peakon solutions of the Camassa–Holm equation, determine whether the conic singularity is related to jumps between solutions of system (12) lying on the same Liouville torus.

evidence.quote: Problem 2.1. Obtain soliton-type solutions of known special cases of BKM systems using this approach.
What are properties of the solutions of these systems obtained by the method of [13]? Which of them can be called finite-gap or soliton solutions?

A particular system and a particular class of intersting solutions is the class of peakon solutions of the Camassa-Holm equation. These solutions have a conic-type singularity. Is the singularity related to ‘jumps’ from one solution of (12) to another under the condition that these solutions belong to the same Liouville torus?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the class of BKM (Bolsinov–Konyaev–Matveev) systems of PDEs, a family of (1+1)-dimensional integrable PDE systems constructed from a pair of compatible Nijenhuis operators, which contains in particular the Korteweg–de Vries (KdV) equation, coupled KdV systems, the Harry Dym equation, coupled Harry Dym systems, the Camassa–Holm equation, multi-component Camassa–Holm systems, the Dullin–Gottwald–Holm equation, and the Kaup–Boussinesq system. There is a known finite-dimensional reduction procedure that associates to such a BKM system a finite-dimensional integrable Hamiltonian system (referred to below as system (∗)) on a symplectic manifold foliated by Liouville tori, such that joint solutions of (∗) produce particular solutions of the original PDE.

(a) Using this finite-dimensional reduction, construct soliton-type solutions for each of the listed special cases (KdV, coupled KdV, Harry Dym, coupled Harry Dym, Camassa–Holm, multi-component Camassa–Holm, Dullin–Gottwald–Holm, Kaup–Boussinesq).

(b) Determine analytic and geometric properties of the PDE solutions produced by this reduction, and decide intrinsic criteria specifying which of them deserve to be called finite-gap solutions and which deserve to be called soliton solutions.

(c) For the Camassa–Holm equation, the peakon solutions exhibit a conic-type singularity in the wave profile. Decide whether this conic singularity can be interpreted as a "jump" between two distinct solutions of the finite-dimensional system (∗) that lie on one and the same Liouville torus; that is, determine whether peakons correspond to a gluing of solution branches of (∗) belonging to a common invariant Liouville torus.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was posed as a research problem within the Nijenhuis Geometry program on BKM systems. A 2026 follow-up establishes jet-density/jet-surjectivity of finite-gap solutions for classes of BKM systems containing Camassa–Holm, advancing the theoretical framework but not constructing the explicit soliton solutions, classifying finite-gap vs. soliton solutions, or resolving the peakon conic-singularity / Liouville-torus jump question. No source verifies a complete solution to (a)–(c).

status_evidence.title: Jet-Density of Finite-Gap Solutions for Classes of BKM Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Finite-gap solutions for BKM systems are constructed via a finite-dimensional Stäckel-type reduction; jet-surjectivity is established for classes containing Camassa–Holm.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work develops finite-gap solutions for BKM systems but does not resolve the explicit soliton construction or peakon/conic-singularity questions.

status_evidence.title: The Geometry of Peaked Solitons and Billiard Solutions of a Class of Integrable PDEs
status_evidence.snippet: Peakon solutions of Camassa–Holm exhibit conic/peaked singularities related to finite-dimensional Hamiltonian reductions.
status_evidence.claim: The geometric interpretation of peakon singularities via finite-dimensional Hamiltonian systems is studied but the specific Liouville-torus jump conjecture remains unverified.
